newsitem.title: USA: Kohlberg Kravis to buy 61 percent of Texas grocery chain.
newsitem.headline: Kohlberg Kravis to buy 61 percent of Texas grocery chain.

text.p: Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. has signed a defintive agreement to buy a majority stake in Randalls Food Markets Inc., a privately-owned grocery chain based in Houston, the companies said Thursday.
Under the agreement, an affiliate of the private investment firm will make a $225 million equity investment in Randalls, which will use the funds to reduce debt, they said.
The deal is expected to close in June, subject to customary closing conditions, they said.

The grocery chain, with fiscal year 1996 revenues of $2.4 billion, operates 54 stores in the Houston area and 16 in the Austin area, all under the Randalls name. It also operates 51 Tom Thumb stores in Dallas/Fort Worth.
Robert R. Onstead Sr. will remain chairman of the company while his son, R. Randall Onstead Jr., will be chief executive.

In an an interview with Reuters, he said Kohlberg Kravis will take a 61 percent stake in the company while his father will continue to be the majority owner of the remaining 39 percent, the holders of which will include the company's employee stock option plan and management.
"The KKR investment will allow us to facilitate the kind of growth we need to embark on in the next five to 10 years," he said.
He said the Kohlberg Kravis investment will be used do pay down debt to strengthen the company's balance sheet.
"We will also use a lot of money to expand some stores, particularly in Dallas," and open new ones, he said.
